title: taxonomy: refine Determinism; add clarifying notes to Control Flow, Workflow Execution, and Handoff
author: chaksaray
inline_text:
@mssumanth — the four terms from our discussion. Summary of what actually changed and why, since two of these turned out not to need a definition change.

## Determinism — real change

Current definition ties Determinism to the whole Workflow, which an LLM-driven Activity fails by construction, exactly where agentic workflows begin. New definition names Determinism as a property of a specific layer (Workflow Execution, Control Flow, or an individual Activity), so a Workflow can be deterministic in Control Flow while containing non-deterministic Activities, without that being a contradiction.

Kept measurement out of the definition, per your explicit ask: the note says the definition takes no position on how Determinism is measured or scored, and cites AVE's `non_determinism` AIVSS factor ("behavioral variability across runs") only as evidence that layer-specific, graded determinism is already load-bearing elsewhere — not as an endorsement of that or any approach.

**Note on PR #55**: I read your Determinism draft there before writing this. It already moved the subject from "Workflow" to "component or execution step," which is a step in this direction, but doesn't yet make the layering explicit. Worth reconciling the two once this lands — happy to update whichever needs it.

## Control Flow — holds, no change; added a note

Re-read this against the "runtime-determined sequencing" concern and concluded the definition itself is fine: "the logic that determines order/branching/etc." is agnostic to whether that logic is fixed at design time or evaluated dynamically by an agent. The actual ambiguity is that a reader might not realize that. Added a note making it explicit and pointing at Orchestration, which already covers *who* does the determining. No definition change.

## Workflow Execution — holds, no change; added a note

Checked whether identity survives mid-execution replanning or retry. It does, by the existing definitions: Lifecycle already covers "the sequence of execution states and transitions... from initiation to completion," and Plan already permits mid-execution modification. A replan is a Lifecycle transition within one Workflow Execution, not a new one. Added a note saying so explicitly; no definition change.

## Handoff — the collision doesn't exist as written text; flagging what's actually true instead

Checked `wg-observability-and-traceability` directly for their Handoff definition. It isn't there — no standalone term entry, only two passing charter mentions of "hand-offs" as an in-scope tracing concern. So there's no real, citable collision between two definitions to reconcile today.

What I did find: Handoff is already jointly claimed by three groups in the central taxonomy (still "pending"), and your own PR #55 is the first real definition attempt. I added a note here summarizing that, quoting #55's proposed wording without copying it into this doc (that's not agreed yet), and recommending Observability review #55 directly rather than this group and Observability drafting in parallel. The two framings I could reconstruct — transfer of responsibility vs. the observable boundary where it happens — read as complementary, not competing, once Observability actually writes theirs down.

---

Reasoning is in the terms file itself (as `**Note:**` blocks under each term) rather than duplicated here at length. Everything above is a pointer to it, not a restatement.
